Christians often use them to picture imputation (one person's debt or sin counted to another), as when Isaiah says 'the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all' and Paul says God 'made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf'. Pairing these passages is the app's illustration, not a link the New Testament makes.

title: The Blood That Cleanses From All Sin & Propitiation

ot.author: Moses, Isaiah & Zechariah
ot.context: On the Day of Atonement the high priest sprinkles blood on the mercy seat (the gold cover of the ark), and atonement is made to cleanse Israel from all their sins; the prophets add pictures of sins washed white and a cleansing fountain.
ot.text: Aaron shall then slaughter the goat for the sin offering for the people and bring its blood behind the veil, and with its blood he must do as he did with the bull’s blood: He is to sprinkle it against the mercy seat and in front of it. … because on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, and you will be clean from all your sins before the LORD. … “Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool. … “On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.
ot.keyPhrase: to cleanse you, and you will be clean from all your sins before the LORD

nt.author: John
nt.context: John presents Jesus as our righteous advocate with the Father and the atoning sacrifice for the sins of the whole world, whose blood cleanses from all sin.
nt.text: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin. … My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One. He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world. … And love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
nt.keyPhrase: the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin

bridge: On the Day of Atonement the high priest sprinkled blood on the mercy seat, the gold cover of the ark (Leviticus 16:15), and God promised, 'you will be clean from all your sins'. 1 John 1:7 closely echoes that promise: 'the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.' Isaiah 1:18 and Zechariah 13:1 add pictures from the prophets: sins made 'as white as snow' and a fountain opened 'to cleanse them from sin and impurity'. John also calls Jesus the 'atoning sacrifice' for our sins (Greek hilasmos, 'propitiation' in older Bibles), a word related to, but not the same as, hilastērion, the Greek Old Testament word for the mercy seat. Christians have long read the Day of Atonement as typology (an institution that foreshadows Christ), and Hebrews 9:11-12 makes that link openly.

title: Walking in Truth and Love

ot.author: David & Moses
ot.context: David prays to walk in God's truth with an undivided heart; the Law calls Israel to love the LORD with all their heart and their neighbor as themselves.
ot.text: Teach me Your way, O LORD, that I may walk in Your truth. Give me an undivided heart, that I may fear Your name. … And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength. … Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
ot.keyPhrase: that I may walk in Your truth

nt.author: John the Elder
nt.context: The elder rejoices that some of the lady's children walk in the truth and reminds his readers of the command they have had from the beginning: love one another.
nt.text: I was overjoyed to find some of your children walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us. And now I urge you, dear lady—not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning—that we love one another. And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the very commandment you have heard from the beginning, that you must walk in love.
nt.keyPhrase: walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us

bridge: The elder is overjoyed to find some of the lady's children 'walking in the truth' and urges her to 'love one another', a command 'we have had from the beginning'. The letter never mentions the Law of Moses: 'from the beginning' most likely means from the start of the readers' faith, when they heard Jesus' command to love one another (John 13:34). Still, the wording has deep Old Testament roots: the psalmist prays 'that I may walk in Your truth', and Israel is told to 'love your neighbor as yourself' and to love the LORD 'with all your heart'. This is a thematic parallel the app draws; 2 John does not quote or clearly allude to these verses.

title: Hospitality to Messengers of the Name & Imitating the Good

ot.author: David, Solomon & the author of Kings
ot.context: Turning from evil to do good (Psalm 34:14), not withholding good when it is in your power (Proverbs 3:27), and the Shunammite woman making a room for the prophet Elisha (2 Kings 4:8-10).
ot.text: Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it. … Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act. … One day Elisha went to Shunem, and a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal. So whenever he would pass by, he would stop there to eat. Then the woman said to her husband, “Behold, now I know that the one who often comes our way is a holy man of God. Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him. Then when he comes to us, he can stay there.”
ot.keyPhrase: Turn away from evil and do good

nt.author: John the Elder
nt.context: John commending Gaius for supporting traveling teachers who went out 'on behalf of the Name', and urging him to imitate what is good.
nt.text: Beloved, you are faithful in what you are doing for the brothers, and especially since they are strangers to you. They have testified to the church about your love. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God. For they went out on behalf of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles. Therefore we ought to support such men, so that we may be fellow workers for the truth. … Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. The one who does good is of God; the one who does evil has not seen God.
nt.keyPhrase: do not imitate what is evil, but what is good

bridge: 3 John quotes none of these Old Testament verses; the links are shared ideas. John's 'do not imitate what is evil, but what is good' recalls 'Turn away from evil and do good' (Psalm 34:14), and Gaius's care for traveling teachers resembles the Shunammite woman's room for Elisha. The teachers went out 'on behalf of the Name' (3 John 1:7). John does not say whose name, though most readers take it as Jesus' name, as in Acts 5:41. If so, John uses for Jesus an expression Israel used with reverence for God: Leviticus 24:11 already speaks of 'the Name', and later Jews called God HaShem (Hebrew for 'the Name') to avoid saying His name.
